Read-only second review (Opus). Not built here.

Verdict: Ready to merge.

Blockers: none.

What I checked, by a read of `git diff origin/main...origin/pr-2940` and of `chamfer_ride.rs` at the head. The PR merges cleanly with `origin/main` (`git merge-tree`). Since the merge base `afbf1590e`, main changed no chamfer code and no chamfer test.

1. The rule. `leans(top, wall)` is true only when the top loop is a translated copy of the wall loop. The vector is the difference of the two area centroids. Then each vertex and each segment mid of each ring must be within `LEAN_SLACK` (1e-4 mm) of the other ring, in the two directions.
   - (a) The box under a tilt is exempt. A prism, sliced by two parallel planes, gives two sections that are exact translates, for all tilts. This is also true for a tessellated cylinder, because each facet is planar. The collinear vertices at different positions do not change the area centroid. The pin `a_wall_leaning_in_the_frame_is_not_a_modelled_chamfer` uses the loops of the fixture.
   - (b) The plate of #2887 is still refused. A bevel on one side moves that side in and leaves the other sides. The area of the top loop is then smaller than the area of the wall loop. A translate keeps the area, so `leans` is false. The extra vertex does not change this. `crates/app/tests/chamfer_partly_bevelled.rs` is not changed. The body gives a mutation run: `leans` replaced by `true` makes the two #2887 unit pins and the new combined pin red.
   - (c) A real partial bevel with a tilt: the bevel removes area, thus `leans` is false and the loop is refused (the safe side). This is pinned by `a_moved_outline_with_one_side_bevelled_still_refuses`. A bevel on one full side, or on two opposite sides, also changes the area, thus no exemption.

2. Tolerances and degenerate input. `LEAN_SLACK` (1e-4 mm) is 500 times smaller than `MATCH_SLACK` (0.05 mm), thus no bevel that `partly_bevelled` reads can hide in it. `centroid` returns `None` for an empty ring (`first()?`) and for a ring with no area (`area.abs() > 1e-12`, plus `is_finite`). A float division by zero gives NaN or inf and no panic. The `% from.len()` in `on` is not evaluated on an empty ring. `near` gives `+inf` for an empty ring, thus `leans` is false. No `unwrap` or `expect` outside the tests.

3. Tests and gate evidence. The two new unit pins cover the rigid shift and the combined case. The #2887 unit pins cover the partial bevel. The body gives the gate on the final source: the quick gate (motion lib, `chamfer_modelled_edge`, `chamfer_partly_bevelled`), `stock_source_holes` by hand (9 passed), and clippy `-D warnings` on `camcraft-motion` and `camcraft-app`. The head has one commit, `4a1007332`. I did not run these.

4. Form. `chamfer_ride.rs` has 381 lines (under 400). The decision file has the required sections. The body has a `Changelog:` line and `Fixes #2936`. The body names #2887 and #2929 with no closing keyword.

Notes (not blocking):

1. Worst case that I can construct for (c). An upright frame and a 60 x 40 plate. The -X side has a modelled 1 x 45 chamfer. The +X side has a 45 degree undercut lip that stands out 1 mm at the top. The Y sides are vertical. Then the top section is `[-29, 31] x [-20, 20]` and the corner section is `[-30, 30] x [-20, 20]`: an exact translate by (1, 0). `leans` is true, `partly_bevelled` returns `None`, and `ride_loops` rides the corner section all round. The chamfer then breaks the sharp Y edges and the lip edge, which the model keeps sharp. This is the defect of #2887. It occurs only when the lip offset is equal to the chamfer offset within 1e-4 mm, so I do not block on it: main is red, and the case needs an exact match. Recommendation: file a `source:agent` follow-up (P3, effort:high). A possible guard is to permit the exemption only when the shift vector is equal to the shift that the operation frame tilt gives (`(top_z - corner_z) * tan(tilt)` in the tilt direction). In an upright frame the expected shift is zero, and this case is then refused again.
2. The decision file says "Thus the new test cannot hide a case of #2887". Note 1 shows a constructed case that it hides. Please change the sentence, for example: "only a part whose sections are exact translates passes, for example a bevel on one side together with an undercut of the same offset on the opposite side; see the follow-up".
3. The quick gate does not select `stock_source_holes` for a change in `motion::machining2d::chamfer_ride`. The author ran it by hand. A Gate map entry for `chamfer_ride` in `stock_source_holes.rs` is a possible P7 follow-up.
4. #2929 (one drafted side) stays open. This PR does not change it, and the decision file says so.
